newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Merrill on supermarket chains.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Merrill on supermarket chains.

text.p: -- Merrill Lynch analyst Gary Vineberg said he downgraded several supermarket chains after Albertson's Inc warned that third and fourth quarter earnings would be below analysts' forecasts.
-- The analyst said he still rates Albertson's as a near-term accumulate and long-term buy after the stock shed 6-1/2 to 38-1/8 on Monday.
-- But Vineberg made the following changes on other stocks:
Winn-Dixie Stores Inc cut to near-term neutral from accumulate and maintained its long-term accumulate.
-- Hannaford Bros Co cut to near-term accumulate from buy and maintained its long-term buy.
-- Kroger Co cut to near-term neutral from accumulate and maintained its long-term accumulate.
-- Safeway Inc downgraded to near-term neutral from accumulate but raised to long-term buy from accumulate.

-- "I made the comments yesterday that the group is getting riskier because of earnings disappointments like at Albertson's, with some lowering prices and not getting the sales they wanted," Vineberg said.
-- He noted the group surged 32 percent this year and lost seven percent on Monday after the Albertson's warning.

-- "I'm neutral on the group and had been positive. With technology stocks running again, people are looking for places to take profits. The signs in supermarkets are not terrible but they are turning more negative," he said.
-- He noted the group has "enormous cap spending budgets and are building a lot of stores. But you can get overstored."
-- As for Safeway, he cut his near-term rating on valuation, noting the stock is up almost 70 percent this year, but upgraded his long-term rating, since "earnings are still strong."
